replies.author: monsterfurby
replies.body:
Yeah. I'm getting a bit exhausted, honestly, by people underappreciating that persistence is the huge, massive, challenge to solve in nearly every GenAI application. Of course, videos are pretty and all, but even those "world models" are just videos loosely wearing the skin of a game. 

Text models got pretty far, but virtually every other discipline is just... way behind there or developing sideways. The best game-focused implementation I have seen have been Skyrim mods, which are doing some real pioneer work for game logic.

comments.author: InsensitiveClown
comments.body: You don't need to imagine a lot. Lots of CG work nowadays is pretty standard layout, simple rendering, which is used to drive the actual AI rendering and shading, constrained to the scene via normalized Z-depth, normals, albedo maps, contour maps, material IDs and object IDs (segmentation passes). The renderer becomes an auxiliary tool providing something essentially similar to old day's AOVs - arbitrary output variables. With the added advantage that you can output your own arbitrary geometric variables and train your own models to infer from them to do things such as style transfer.
